newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end higher, consolidation seen.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end higher, consolidation seen.

text.p: Taiwan stocks closed slightly higher on Wednesday in slow trade and brokers said the market was likely to stay in a consolidation phase in the near term.
Large scale trading was deterred by recent selling by foreign institutions but brokers noted minor bargain hunting now that the index has lost some 200 points since mid-October.
"Taiwan's September export orders and industrial output figures were both good and there is no reason to be pessmistic," said Barry Lin of China Securities Investment Trust.
The weighted index finished up 10.76 points -- a scant 0.17 percent -- to 6,437.06. Turnover was a slow T$33.6 billion.

Foreign orders for Taiwan goods rose 7.11 percent in September from a year earlier to US$10.513 billion, a monthly record high, the economics ministry said on Monday. Industrial output rose 3.90 percent over the same period, it said.

As many economists have been forecasting a recovery to start in the fourth quarter of 1996 and several major Taiwan banks cut interest rates recently, brokers said they were optimistic over the island's liquidity situation.
"The consolidation may last for some time, but there is no bad news ahead to pull the market further down," said Chen Han-chung of Yungli Securities.

Low-priced textiles and foundamentals-backed electronics shares attracted minor buying. Textile stock Hualon rose 70 cents or 2.8 percent to T$25.7 and Shingkong Synthetic Fibre gained 40 cents or 1.8 percent to T$23.0.
Brokers saw strong support for the market at 6,400 points.
"If the index falls below that level, bargain buying should emerge and push share prices up again," Lin said.
